name: Panera Bread Design System
summary: Bakery-warm ordering UI kit: cream-and-green iOS design tokens, rewards card, and menu-to-checkout components for a QSR app.
description: A deep SwiftUI-ready prompt for a warm, bakery-style food-ordering interface built around a single green action color, cream card surfaces, and a loyalty rewards banner.

whatYouGet: A full warm-bakery color and type ladder (cream surfaces, single green CTA, gold reward accent) ready to drop into Color/Font extensions
The MyPanera rewards banner, quantity stepper, and sticky Add-to-Order bar specified down to the pixel and easing curve
House rules that keep the ordering flow (menu card → item detail → cart) consistent instead of inventing a new pattern per screen
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in warm, appetite-forward QSR and bakery-café ordering apps. You think in terms of food photography hierarchy, loyalty-program psychology, and tactile ordering flows, and you deliver production-ready SwiftUI, not mockups.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (light / dark):
- Canvas: #FFFFFF warm white / #14140F warm near-black (never cold gray or pure black)
- Card surface: #F4EFE1 cream / #1E1E18
- Elevated panel: #FAF6EC oat / #28281F
- Divider: #E7E0CF / #33332A
- Text primary: #2A2A1F warm dark / #F3EFE4
- Text secondary: #6C6655 / #B4AE9C
- Primary action green: #4C8B2B, bright/dark-mode variant #6BBE45, pressed #3C6E22
- Green tint wash: #EAF3E3 / #1E2A18
- Photographic accents: bread tan #D8B271, soup orange #E07A2F, berry red #B0324B, gold reward star #F2B705, Sip Club coffee #5A3A22
- Error #D6452F / #E0594B

Typography: Poppins (ExtraBold/Bold/SemiBold) carries brand/display moments — screen titles 32pt/800, item names 15-18pt/600, prices 14pt/700. Inter (Regular/Medium/SemiBold) carries body, meta, calorie counts, tab labels, and chips. Weight ladder is concentrated at 400/500/600/700/800 with no thin or hairline weights.

Spacing/geometry: 4pt base unit, scale 4-8-12-16-18-20-24-28-32-40-56. Radius scale: 0pt hero photos, 6pt small tags, 10pt thumbnails, 14pt menu photo cards, 18pt reward card and sheets, 24pt modal top corners, 999pt (full pill) for every button/toggle/search field, 50% for circular add buttons and avatars.

Distinctive patterns:
1. MyPanera rewards card — a green gradient (#4C8B2B → #6BBE45 at 135°) banner pinned near the top of Home with an uppercase label, a bold headline, a progress track at rgba(255,255,255,0.28) with a white fill, and a trailing chevron.
2. Menu item row — leading square photo (92pt, 14pt radius), item name, 2-line clamped description, price, and a 30pt green circular '+' add button.
3. Quantity stepper — pill container in oat/dark-surface fill with a 1pt divider-color border, '−'/'+' glyphs in the green, centered count, 44pt tap zones.
4. Sticky Add-to-Order bar — full-width green pill fixed above the tab bar showing 'Add to Order · $price'.
5. Reward star tag — an inline '★ FREE WITH n PTS' label in gold + green text on redeemable menu items.
6. Pickup/Delivery segmented pill toggle at the top of the cart, selected segment filled green.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Green is the ONLY action color in the entire app — never introduce a second accent for CTAs, active tabs, or the rewards progress arc.
2. The canvas and its card surfaces must stay warm (cream/oat/warm-near-black) — reject pure white, cold gray, or pure black at every step, including dark mode.
3. Body and primary text are warm dark (#2A2A1F), never pure black — this is what keeps the bakery feeling tangible rather than clinical.
4. Every button and toggle is a fully-rounded pill (999pt radius) — no sharp-cornered buttons anywhere in this system.
5. Gold (#F2B705) is reserved exclusively for reward, Sip Club, and rating moments — using it decoratively dilutes its meaning.
6. Food photography must always be the largest, most prominent element on any card — chrome recedes, the photo sells.
7. Calorie counts always sit next to the price on menu items and item-detail headers — never omit or bury this pairing.
8. Motion stays gentle: 120-600ms ease-out transitions with soft haptics on add-to-order, stepper taps, and reward unlocks — never sharp or bouncy beyond a subtle scale-bounce.
9. Shadows are warm-tinted (brown-amber rgba values), never neutral gray, so elevation reads as natural depth on the cream surfaces.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / brand name: [your bakery or QSR brand]
- Primary food category (e.g. sandwiches, soups, baked goods, bowls): [fill in]
- Loyalty program name and reward mechanic (points, visits, stamps): [fill in]
- Core menu categories to support in the ordering flow: [fill in, e.g. Soups, Sandwiches, Salads, Bakery, Drinks]
- Number of customization options per typical item (bread choice, add-ons, sauces): [fill in]
- Pickup and/or delivery support: [fill in]
- Existing brand hex (if you already have one green/accent to reuse instead of Panera's): [fill in or 'use as-is']
- Target iOS minimum version: [fill in, e.g. iOS 16+]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete Color and Font SwiftUI extension file implementing the palette and type ladder above, adapted to the brand name and any custom accent supplied.
2. The MyPanera-style rewards banner component (or renamed for the given loyalty program) with the gradient, progress bar, and headline/subtext layout, including a working preview with sample data.
3. The menu item row/card component with photo, name, clamped description, price, optional reward tag, and circular add button, ready to drop into a List or LazyVStack.
4. The item-detail screen skeleton: full-bleed hero photo, transparent-to-opaque top nav, customization rows, quantity stepper, and the sticky Add-to-Order bar.
5. The 5-tab bottom navigation bar wired to the brand's action color, with SF Symbol suggestions per tab.
6. A short dark-mode notes section explaining which tokens must swap (and which, like the accent green, should brighten rather than invert) to preserve legibility.
7. A do's/don'ts checklist tailored to the supplied brand so a second engineer can self-review before merging.
</what_to_give_me>

name: Resy Design System
summary: Editorial dark-mode reservation UI kit: pure-black canvas, serif restaurant names, and a red-outlined slot-booking grid.
description: A deep SwiftUI-ready prompt for a magazine-style, dark-first restaurant reservation app built on typographic contrast, a disciplined single red accent, and a signature slot-availability grid.

whatYouGet: A pure-black, editorial color and type system pairing a display serif with a functional sans, ready for Color/Font extensions
The signature reservation slot grid (outlined/solid/dashed states) and date-strip picker specified with exact radii and states
House rules protecting the serif/sans split, the red-outline booking convention, and Resy's flat, hairline-bordered depth model
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in editorial, dark-first hospitality and reservation apps. You think in terms of magazine-grade typographic contrast, curated discovery feeds, and booking-availability UI, and you deliver production-ready SwiftUI, not mockups.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (dark-first is the brand; light is a secondary inversion):
- Canvas: #000000 pure black (dark) / #FFFFFF (light inversion)
- Surface 1/2/3 (dark): #121212 / #1C1C1C / #242424
- Divider (dark): #262626
- Text primary: #F5F5F5 near-white (never pure white) / #101010 on light
- Text secondary: #9E9E9E / #6B6B6B
- Primary reservation color: #C73E3A, bright/active-tab variant #E2504B, pressed #A8302D
- Notify/waitlist amber: #D99A2B
- Rating/curation gold: #C9A24B
- Confirmed green: #4FA773 dark / #2F8C56 light

Typography: Playfair Display (serif, 700-800, italic for editorial voice) is reserved for restaurant names, feature titles, and taglines. Inter (400-700) carries every functional element — metadata, slot times, seating labels, buttons, nav. Restaurant name at 27pt/700, section headers 22pt/700 in Inter, italic editorial tagline 15pt/400, slot time 14pt/700, seating label 9pt/600 uppercase.

Spacing/geometry: 4pt base, scale 4-8-9-12-16-18-20-22-24-32-40. Radius scale: 0pt hero photos, 2pt rating-mark container, 4pt small badges, 8pt buttons/search bar/photo cards, 10pt reservation slot chips and date cells, 16pt sheet top corners, 999pt reserved only for the Notify chip and daypart toggle, 50% circles.

Distinctive patterns:
1. Reservation slot chip system — available slots render transparent-filled with a 1pt red border; the recommended/primary slot is solid red; a sold-out slot becomes a dashed 1pt border amber 'Notify' chip. This three-state contrast is the product's signature.
2. Horizontal date strip — 60pt cells with weekday + date number, default dark-surface fill with a hairline border, selected day solid red.
3. Editorial restaurant detail — full-bleed photo carousel, serif restaurant name, gold '★ 9.4' rating mark, italic serif tagline, then the date strip and slot grid beneath an uppercase eyebrow.
4. Seating-type label under every slot ('Dining Room' / 'Bar' / 'Counter' / 'Patio' / 'Chef's Counter').
5. Notify (waitlist) surface — a dedicated tab and dashed-border chip pattern for sold-out tables, promoted as a first-class parallel path to booking.
6. Hairline borders (#262626), not shadows, are the elevation cue — shadows are nearly invisible on pure black.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. The canvas is pure black by design, not an optional dark mode — treat black as the primary brand surface and the light inversion as secondary.
2. Restaurant names and any editorial title always use the display serif — never render a restaurant name in the sans; the serif/sans split IS the brand.
3. Red is the only reservation color — never introduce a second hue for booking, selection, or active-tab states.
4. Available slots must be OUTLINED, never solid; only the primary/recommended slot is filled solid red — this outline/solid contrast is the whole signal and must not be flattened.
5. Every slot must show its seating type beneath the time — never omit it, since the product books specific seatings, not just time windows.
6. Sold-out slots become dashed amber Notify affordances, never a generic disabled gray — Notify is a first-class booking path with its own tab, not an error state.
7. Use hairline borders for elevation instead of drop shadows — shadows are close to invisible against pure black and will look like a rendering mistake if relied upon.
8. Keep geometry crisp (8-10pt radii) rather than pill-soft except where the scale explicitly calls for a 999pt pill (Notify chip, daypart toggle) — Resy's shape language is editorial, not soft.
9. Reserve muted gold strictly for the rating mark and the curated collection — never use it as a general highlight color.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App/brand name: [your reservation or dining brand]
- Primary booking unit (table, seat, experience slot): [fill in]
- Seating types offered (e.g. Dining Room, Bar, Patio, Private): [fill in]
- Curated/saved-collection feature name (Resy calls it 'Hit List'): [fill in]
- Waitlist/notify mechanic details: [fill in]
- Rating scale used (e.g. /10, /5 stars, editorial score only): [fill in]
- Whether light mode is required as a secondary theme: [fill in]
- Target iOS minimum version: [fill in]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete Color and Font SwiftUI extension implementing the palette and Playfair Display / Inter type ladder, adapted to the given brand.
2. The reservation slot grid component covering all three states (available/primary/sold-out-notify) with correct radii, borders, and press/select animation.
3. The horizontal date strip component with default/selected cell states and a month-sheet trigger affordance.
4. The editorial restaurant/venue detail screen: photo carousel header, serif name, rating mark, italic tagline, eyebrow, date strip, and slot grid assembled in order.
5. The 5-tab bottom navigation bar with the Notify tab included as a first-class destination.
6. A confirmation card layout (serif name, date/time, party size, seating type, confirmation code) with its motion spec.
7. A short note on adapting the whole system to a light-mode inversion without breaking the serif/sans and outline/solid conventions.
</what_to_give_me>

whatYouGet: A warm-retail color and type system (Siren Green action color, forest-green dark canvas, gold rewards accent) ready for Color/Font extensions
The Stars progress ring and 5-pill size selector specified with exact stroke widths, gradients, and slide animations
House rules protecting the rewards-first hierarchy, the non-black dark mode, and the calm hospitality tone of the palette
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in retail loyalty-driven ordering apps for coffee and quick-service chains. You think in terms of daily-habit reward loops, drink-customization flows, and calm hospitality tone, and you deliver production-ready SwiftUI, not mockups.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (light / dark):
- Canvas: #F9F9F9 warm white (softer than pure white) / #1E3932 house green (a deep forest tone, NOT black or gray)
- Card surface: #FFFFFF / #2D4A43
- Elevated surface: #F1F1F1 / #3B5852
- Divider: #E8E8E8 / #3A4F48
- Text primary: #000000 (true black used deliberately for body) / #FFFFFF
- Text secondary: #595959 / #C9CDCB
- Primary brand green: #00704A, pressed #00563A
- Secondary dark brand green: #1E3932 (the dark-canvas color itself)
- Soft mint accent: #D4E9E2 (reward-moment tint, promo backgrounds)
- Gold tier/reward: #CBA258, gradient variant #C1A265, ring gradient #CBA258 → #E4C896 → #CBA258
- Alert red #DD3333, warning amber #F5A623, info blue #006FCF (used sparingly)

Typography: a proprietary humanist sans (documented here as 'SoDo Sans' lineage) carries every role, with weights concentrated at 400/600/700/800 — ExtraBold (800) reserved for the Stars count and hero moments. Stars hero count is 48pt/800, screen titles 28pt/700, size-selector labels 13pt/600 with 0.2pt tracking, body 15pt/400 at a generous 1.45 line-height. Numerals are tabular throughout so Stars counts and prices align in columns.

Spacing/geometry: 4pt base, scale 4-8-12-16-20-24-32-40-48. Radius scale: 4pt small badges, 12pt modal inner cards, 16pt category/reward/offer cards, 20pt hero cards, 22-26pt pill buttons and the size-selector pills, 50% for the Stars ring, stepper buttons, and tab icons.

Distinctive patterns:
1. Stars rewards dashboard — a 180pt circular progress ring, 12pt stroke, track in a light neutral, fill a gold gradient starting at 12 o'clock and sweeping clockwise, with the Stars count centered in 48pt ExtraBold gold and a 'Stars until reward' subtitle beneath.
2. Size selector pill row — five pills (e.g. Short/Tall/Grande/Venti/Trenta), 36pt tall, inactive transparent with a hairline border, active filled brand green with white text; a small size-scaled cup icon sits above each label; selecting slides the active fill to the new position.
3. Category grid card — 2:3 photo-led tile, 16pt radius, bottom gradient scrim for label legibility, entire card tappable.
4. Customization stepper — a '− n +' pattern with 36pt circular outlined buttons flanking a centered tabular count, used for syrup pumps and shot counts.
5. Scan-to-pay hero — a white card with a centered barcode, a numeric code beneath it in tabular type, and a balance readout with a reload pill; the barcode auto-refreshes on an interval.
6. Reward tile banner — a full-width soft-mint card pairing a gold star + points count with a redeem pill.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never use pure black for the dark-mode canvas — the deep forest-green dark tone is load-bearing brand identity, not a placeholder for gray or black.
2. Place the Stars (or renamed rewards) progress ring at the very top of the home/landing tab — it is the daily habit hook and must never be buried below other content.
3. Reserve the brand green for every primary CTA and never introduce a second loud accent color competing with it.
4. Gold is exclusively the rewards/Stars/tier color — it must never be rendered as plain yellow or orange, and must never decorate non-reward UI.
5. The size-selector (or equivalent core customization) pill row is the mental model of ordering — never collapse it into a plain dropdown or picker wheel.
6. Keep the weight ladder to 400/600/700/800 only, with 800 reserved for the rewards count and hero display moments — do not introduce thin or light weights anywhere.
7. Motion stays calm: 250-400ms with spring dampings around 0.7-0.85 — avoid sharp, bouncy, or attention-grabbing animation outside the rewards-earned moment.
8. Use tabular numerals wherever money, points, or counts appear so columns of numbers always align cleanly.
9. Route haptic feedback by intent: light on pills/steppers, medium on the primary CTA, success specifically on rewards-earned and order-placed moments — never generic haptics everywhere.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App/brand name: [your coffee or QSR brand]
- Rewards currency name and redemption mechanic (points, stars, stamps): [fill in]
- Product sizes to support in the customizer (and their labels): [fill in]
- Customization options per drink/item (milk, syrups, shots, toppings): [fill in]
- In-store pay/scan flow required: [fill in yes/no + details]
- Store-locator requirement: [fill in]
- Primary brand hex if different from the reference green: [fill in]
- Target iOS minimum version: [fill in]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete Color and Font SwiftUI extension implementing the palette and type ladder, adapted to the given brand's rewards currency name and any custom accent.
2. The Stars-style circular progress ring component with gradient stroke, animated fill, and centered count/subtitle, plus a working preview.
3. The size-selector pill row component with the sliding active-fill animation and size-scaled icon treatment.
4. The category grid card and drink/item detail screen (hero photo, customization stepper rows, sticky primary CTA with embedded price).
5. The scan-to-pay or equivalent screen if requested in the_project, including the balance/reload pattern.
6. The 5-tab bottom navigation bar with a center 'scan' or equivalent anchor tab if relevant to the brand.
7. A short motion/haptics reference table mapping each interaction to its duration, easing, and haptic type.
</what_to_give_me>

name: Swiggy Design System
summary: A crave-and-tap food delivery UI kit: photo-forward orange-accented restaurant cards, veg/non-veg marks, and a floating cart bar.
description: A deep SwiftUI-ready prompt for an appetite-driven, high-density food delivery app built on a single loud accent color, a trust-signaling rating chip, and mandatory dietary marks.

whatYouGet: A photo-forward color and type system with one loud accent color and a semantic green/amber rating chip, ready for Color/Font extensions
The restaurant card, dish row, floating ADD button, and cart bar specified with exact scrim gradients, overlaps, and morph animations
House rules protecting the single-accent discipline, mandatory veg/non-veg marks, and the dashed-divider (not boxed-card) layout language
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in high-velocity, photo-driven food delivery marketplaces for dense urban markets. You think in terms of scan-speed trust signals, appetite-triggering imagery, and rapid multi-vertical navigation, and you deliver production-ready SwiftUI, not mockups.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (light / dark):
- Canvas: #FFFFFF / #121212 near-black (never pure #000000)
- Surface 1/2: #F4F4F6 / #1C1C1E, #ECECEE / #2A2A2A
- Divider: #E2E2E7 / #2C2C2E (rendered dashed on card footers and dish rows)
- Text primary: #02060C / #F2F2F2
- Text secondary: #686B78 / #A0A0A0
- Single hero accent: #FC8019, pressed #E06D0C, 10% tint wash #FC80191A
- Rating scale: green #48C479 (≥4.0), amber #DB7C38 (3.0-3.9), red #E84A4A (<3.0, also error)
- Vertical accents (re-theme per section): grocery magenta-purple #982C61, table-booking red #D7385E
- Offer gradient: #FC8019 → #D7385E

Typography: a heavy geometric-humanist display face (documented as ProximaNova lineage) carries titles, restaurant names, and offer badges at weight 700-800; a neutral grotesque UI face carries body, dish names, prices, and metadata. Screen title 32pt/800, restaurant card name 18pt/800, dish title 15pt/600, price 14pt/600 tabular. Primary CTAs and the ADD button are always UPPERCASE with +0.2-0.3pt tracking.

Spacing/geometry: 4pt base, scale 4-8-12-16-20-24-32-40-48-64. Card vertical gap is a deliberately generous 22pt so each restaurant reads as a discrete decision. Radius scale: 6pt rating chips, 8pt filter/offer chips, 10-12pt buttons/search/form fields/ADD button, 16pt restaurant photos and dish thumbnails, 20pt bottom sheets, 500pt pill for steppers/toggles.

Distinctive patterns:
1. Photo-forward restaurant card — full-bleed 16:10 hero image with a bottom scrim gradient (transparent to ~78% black) carrying a bold white offer line, a rating chip + ETA row beneath, and a dashed-divider footer carrying a free-delivery/coupon line in the accent color.
2. Rating chip — a small pill, green/amber/red by score, containing a white star glyph and the numeric score, always positioned immediately left of the ETA/distance metadata (the first thing users scan).
3. Veg/non-veg mark — a 16pt bordered square with a centered green dot (veg) or red/maroon triangle (non-veg), mandatory on every dish row.
4. Floating 'ADD' button — a green-outlined pill that bottom-overlaps the square dish thumbnail by roughly 12pt with a soft shadow so it visually floats above the food photo; tapping morphs it into a bordered quantity stepper.
5. Sticky location header — a leading pin icon, a 'Home ⌄' style title with the delivery address beneath, and a trailing circular avatar.
6. Floating cart bar — a solid accent-colored bar pinned above the tab bar showing item count and running total, sliding up with a spring when the first item is added.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Use exactly one loud hero accent color for CTAs, active tab, icons, and footer links — never introduce a second competing bright color in the base experience.
2. The rating chip's color must always be earned by the actual score (green ≥4.0, amber 3.0-3.9, red below) — never hardcode a chip color independent of the number it displays.
3. Every dish row must carry a veg/non-veg mark — this is a hard content requirement, not a decorative option, and must never be omitted even in a compact layout.
4. Card and row separators are dashed hairlines, not boxed cards or heavy borders — the whole system avoids nesting content in bordered containers.
5. The ADD button always overlaps the dish image and carries a visible shadow so it reads as a floating, tappable control distinct from the flat list around it.
6. Primary CTA and ADD labels are UPPERCASE with positive letter-spacing — sentence-case, timid button copy breaks the tone of this system.
7. Food photography must stay full-saturation and undimmed in dark mode — only the surrounding chrome darkens, never the imagery.
8. When the product has multiple verticals (e.g. delivery vs. grocery vs. bookings), re-theme only the accent color per vertical while keeping the identical card and list grammar — never redesign the layout per vertical.
9. Keep motion fast and functional (150-320ms) and tied directly to the order flow — avoid decorative or slow transitions anywhere in the ordering path.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App/brand name: [your delivery marketplace brand]
- Primary vertical(s) supported (food delivery, groceries, bookings, etc.): [fill in]
- Whether veg/non-veg or another dietary-mark convention is legally/culturally required in your market: [fill in]
- Filter chip set for the restaurant/listing feed (e.g. rating, time, price, dietary): [fill in]
- Offer/discount mechanics to support (percentage off, free delivery, coupon codes): [fill in]
- Live order tracking requirement: [fill in]
- Primary accent hex if different from the reference orange: [fill in]
- Target iOS minimum version: [fill in]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete Color and Font SwiftUI extension implementing the palette (including the semantic rating scale) and type ladder, adapted to the given brand and accent.
2. The photo-forward restaurant/listing card component with scrim, offer text, rating chip, and dashed-divider footer.
3. The dish/menu-item row with veg/non-veg mark, description clamp, and the floating ADD-button-to-stepper morph animation.
4. The sticky location/search header and the horizontally scrollable filter chip row.
5. The floating cart bar component with slide-up spring animation and live total updates.
6. The bottom tab bar wired for the supported verticals, including per-vertical accent re-theming if multiple verticals were specified.
7. A short motion/haptics reference table (ADD morph, cart bar reveal, filter select, pull-to-refresh) with exact durations and easing.
</what_to_give_me>

description: A deep SwiftUI-ready prompt for a bold, gradient-driven quick-service app centered on a step-by-step box/meal customizer, a violet-tinted dark canvas, and a yellow value accent.

whatYouGet: A violet-tinted dark color system with a signature purple-to-magenta gradient and a disciplined yellow value accent, ready for Color/Font extensions
The numbered step-pill row, box-preview hero, and radio/stepper option rows specified with exact gradients, glow blooms, and transition timings

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in bold, gamified quick-service ordering apps that center on step-by-step build/customization flows. You think in terms of gradient-driven brand energy, dark-canvas neon aesthetics, and playful configurability, and you deliver production-ready SwiftUI, not mockups.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (dark-first primary / light secondary):
- Canvas: #0E0A14 purple-tinted near-black (dark, primary) / #FFFFFF (light, secondary)
- Surface 1/2: #1A1322 / #261B32 (dark), #F6F2F8 / #EDE6F1 (light)
- Divider: #34273F dark / #E3D9EA light
- Text primary: #F4EFF7 violet-tinted near-white / #1F1626 on light
- Text secondary: #A99BB6 / #6E6079
- Brand gradient: linear-gradient(120deg, #702082 0% → #C72BC8 100%) — this gradient IS the brand, not a flat color
- Flat purple fallback: #702082, bright/mid #8A2BA0, electric magenta #C72BC8, magenta pressed #A8239F
- Value/energy accent: Hot Sauce Yellow #FFC700 — text rendered on it is always a deep plum-black #2A1530, never white
- Heat accents: Fire Orange #FF6A1A, Hot Pink #E928A0
- Success/step-done green #36C275, error #FF4D6D

Typography: a clean, techy geometric sans (documented as a Sora-class substitute) carries all UI. Screen titles 32pt/800, builder/customizer titles 26pt/800, option names 15pt/600, prices/totals 15pt/800 tabular. Every builder or section title is preceded by a yellow, UPPERCASE, +1pt-tracked eyebrow — a signature editorial tic.

Spacing/geometry: 4pt base, scale 4-8-12-16-20-24-32-40-48-64. Radius scale: 6pt tiny tags, 10pt inline chips, 12-14pt buttons/fields/menu cards, 20pt the box-preview hero panel, 28pt bottom sheets, 999pt pill for step pills/Add pills/status chips/steppers, 50% circles.

Distinctive patterns:

<house_rules>
1. The purple-to-magenta gradient is the brand identity on screen — never flatten it to a single solid color for primary CTAs, the active step, or the box hero.

8. Keep motion punchy and quick (150-300ms) tied directly to the build/order actions — a brightness-flash on CTA press, a step-pill cross-fade, and a box-hero morph are the expected vocabulary, not slow fades.
9. Never let food imagery desaturate against the neon chrome — the stage is dark and expressive, but the product photography stays vivid.

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in bright, high-trust, photo-first food delivery marketplaces. You think in terms of clean commercial typography, disciplined single-accent action systems, and real-time map tracking UX, and you deliver production-ready SwiftUI, not mockups.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (light default / dark supported):
- Canvas: #FFFFFF pure white (default, photo-first) / #000000 (dark, neutrals only invert)
- Surface: #F3F3F3 / #1C1C1E, Surface 2: #EEEEEE / #2C2C2E
- Divider: #E8E8E8 / #2C2C2E
- Text primary: #000000 / #FFFFFF
- Text secondary: #6B6B6B / #A6A6A6, tertiary #A6A6A6
- Single accent: #06C167 green, pressed #05A658, tint #E7F8EF — this exact hue stays identical in dark mode, only neutrals invert
- Rating star: rendered near-black, deliberately NOT yellow — ratings stay monochrome and quiet
- Busy/surge amber #FF8A00, error red #E11900

Typography: a tight, confident geometric-grotesque brand face (documented as an Uber-Move-class substitute, Inter fallback) at weights 400/500/700 only — no thin, no semibold-as-light, no black weight. Restaurant header name 30pt/700 with negative tracking, restaurant card name 17pt/700, metadata row 14pt/400 in secondary gray, price/CTA label 16pt/700. All-caps reserved strictly for small eyebrow labels, never for restaurant or item names.

Spacing/geometry: 4pt base, scale 4-8-12-16-20-24-32-40-52-64. Feed cards get 24pt vertical breathing room; sections get 32pt. Radius scale: 0pt full-bleed hero photo and map, 8pt small chips, 12pt restaurant/item photos and primary buttons and search bar (a friendlier radius than most competitors), 16pt bottom sheets and promo banners, 500pt full pill for category/filter pills, 50% circles.

Distinctive patterns:
1. Photo-first restaurant card — a borderless, shadowless 16:9 hero photo with the name, a monochrome star rating, ETA, and delivery fee stacked in tight rows directly beneath it on the plain white canvas; the photo's own framing provides all the separation.
2. Sticky cart bar — a solid green bar pinned above the tab bar showing a count badge, 'View cart', and the running total, sliding up with a spring the moment the first item is added.
3. Live map order tracking — a full-screen map with a near-black route polyline and a green courier marker that eases smoothly (~1 second) between location updates, under a draggable white sheet with an ETA headline and a green multi-step progress stepper.
4. Category pill row — a horizontally scrolling row directly beneath the search bar, unselected pills neutral gray, the selected pill filling solid green with white text.
5. Cart-count bump — adding an item flashes green on the '+' control and scales the cart badge (1.0 → 1.25 → 1.0) as tactile confirmation.
6. The active tab is rendered near-black/white, never green — green is reserved exclusively for action surfaces so it never loses its 'this is an action' meaning.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Reserve the single green accent strictly for primary actions and selected states (Add, cart bar, active pill, Track CTA) — never use it for the active tab, which stays near-black/white.
2. Keep the accent hue identical between light and dark mode — only the neutral canvas and surfaces invert; the green itself never changes.
3. Restaurant and menu-item cards are borderless and shadowless on the canvas — never add a card border or drop shadow around food photography; the photo's own edge is the frame.
4. Star ratings render in a monochrome near-black tone, never yellow or gold — this keeps merchandising quiet so the green accent is the only thing that reads as 'action.'
5. The sticky cart bar must remain visible with its live count and total any time the cart is non-empty while browsing a menu — never let it disappear behind other content.
6. Typography weights are limited to 400/500/700 — do not introduce thin, black, or semibold-as-a-substitute-for-regular anywhere in the system.
7. Use the friendlier 12pt radius on buttons and photos (16pt on sheets) rather than a sharper geometric radius — this softness is part of the brand's approachable, commercial tone.
8. The live map courier marker eases smoothly over roughly one second between position updates — it must never jump or snap, since motion on the map is the primary feedback mechanism post-order.
9. All-caps type is reserved for small eyebrow labels only — never apply it to a restaurant name, menu item, or section header.
</house_rules>

name: Yelp Design System
summary: A trust-engine review UI kit: a rationed red accent, a brand-asset 5-star control, and section-band structured business pages.
description: A deep SwiftUI-ready prompt for a review-and-discovery app built around a disciplined single red accent, a half-star rating system, and gray section bands instead of bordered cards.

whatYouGet: A clean white color and type system with a strictly rationed red accent and a warm orange-red star rating, ready for Color/Font extensions
The 5-star rating control, review card, and business-header block specified with exact sizes, half-star logic, and vote-action states
House rules protecting the rationed-red discipline, the mandatory rating-plus-review-count pairing, and the section-band layout language
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in review-and-discovery platforms where trust signals must be scanned in under a second. You think in terms of dense-list scannability, brand-asset rating controls, and structural (not card-based) page chunking, and you deliver production-ready SwiftUI, not mockups.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (light / dark):
- Canvas: #FFFFFF pure white / #161616 near-black (never pure black)
- Surface gray: #F5F5F5 / #1E1E1E, section band: #F0F0F0 / #0C0C0C
- Divider: #E0E0E0 / #303030
- Text primary: #2B2B2B / #E6E6E6
- Text secondary: #6E6E6E / #A8A8A8
- Interactive accent: #FF1A1A, logo/brand variant #D32323, pressed #B81E1E — rationed to primary CTA, active tab, and logomark only
- Rating star filled: #F25C05 warm orange-red (identical in both light and dark), empty #E3E3E0 / #3A3A3A
- Link blue #0073BB / #4FA3D9, open/success green #2DA44E, closed/error #E03E3E, warning #D9730D, Elite badge accent #A2231D / #C24A4A

Typography: Open Sans carries the entire system, tuned for scanning rather than reading — screen title 32pt/800, business name 24pt/800, section header 20pt/700, review body 14pt/400 at a generous 1.55 line-height, but high-frequency metadata (dates, location, vote labels) is bumped to weight 600 at 12-13pt so it stays legible small. Numbers (ratings, review counts, prices) are always weight 700 even at small sizes.

Spacing/geometry: 4pt base, scale 4-8-12-16-20-24-32-40-48-64. Content inset 16pt; review cards use 16pt vertical padding separated by dividers, never card borders. Radius scale: 4pt photo-grid thumbnails, 8pt buttons/search/input fields, 12pt sheets/modals, 500pt pill for category chips and filter pills, 50% circles for avatars and floating header buttons.

Distinctive patterns:
1. 5-star rating control — a brand-asset component, not a generic widget: five glyphs with a 2pt gap, filled in a warm orange-red identical across light and dark, empty in flat gray, supporting half-star increments (never finer than 0.5); a rating must always be paired with its review count nearby.
2. Business detail page — a full-bleed photo header (~184pt) with a photo-count chip, then a tight header block (name, star row, review-count link, price-band-and-category line, open/closed hours line), an action row (primary review CTA + ghost icon buttons), and a scroll of review cards below.
3. Review card — no border or shadow, separated by a hairline divider: circular avatar (photo or colored-gradient monogram), reviewer name + location + review count sub-line, a star row + date, the review body, and a row of three named vote actions that turn the accent color once tapped.
4. Section bands — 8pt full-bleed gray (or near-black on dark) strips chunk the long detail scroll into sections instead of using bordered cards.
5. Category filter chip — a pill with a small accent-stroked glyph; the selected chip flips to a solid accent fill.
6. Price band ($ $$ $$$ $$$$) — rendered purely in neutral text weight, the 'active' glyphs darker than the rest; this is metadata and is never colored.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Ration the single accent color to exactly the primary CTA, the active tab, and the logomark — never let a second accent-colored button appear on the same screen, or the primary action loses its meaning.
2. The filled star in the rating control is a warm orange-red, not pure yellow and not the interactive brand red — keep this hue identical in both light and dark mode so ratings remain instantly recognizable.
3. Never show a rating without its review count next to it — a bare star number is explicitly untrustworthy in this system's logic and must not ship without the count.
4. Round all displayed ratings to the nearest half-star — never render a rating as a more-precise fractional fill.
5. Chunk long detail pages with full-bleed section bands, not bordered or shadowed cards — the whole system relies on structure (dividers, bands) rather than elevation for hierarchy.
6. Never bold review body copy — body text stays at regular weight; only names, headers, and numeric data get heavy weight.
7. The price-band glyphs ($ $$ $$$ $$$$) are neutral metadata and must never be tinted with the accent, success, or error colors.
8. Vote or reaction actions (e.g. helpful/funny/cool-style labels) always show an icon plus a count and shift to the accent color only once the user has voted — never colored by default.
9. Keep motion quiet (120-300ms ease-out) with a soft haptic on each rating increment and a slightly stronger haptic reserved for higher-commitment actions like check-in.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App/brand name: [your review/discovery platform]
- Primary review target (restaurants, services, businesses in general): [fill in]
- Rating scale (5-star with halves, /10, thumbs, etc.): [fill in]
- Named vote/reaction actions on a review (e.g. Helpful/Funny/Cool or your own set): [fill in]
- Category/filter taxonomy for discovery: [fill in]
- Whether a reviewer-tier or 'elite' badge system is needed: [fill in]
- Primary accent hex if different from the reference red: [fill in]
- Target iOS minimum version: [fill in]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete Color and Font SwiftUI extension implementing the palette and type ladder, adapted to the given brand and accent.
2. The 5-star (or equivalent) rating control component supporting half-increments, both display and interactive/input modes.
3. The review card component with avatar, identity line, star+date row, clamped body text, and the named vote-action row.
4. The business/listing detail header block: photo header with counter chip, name, rating+count, category/price line, and hours status.
5. The category filter chip row and a bottom filter sheet layout.
6. The 5-tab bottom navigation bar with a center emphasized 'write/contribute' tab.
7. A short accent-usage audit checklist confirming the accent color never appears more than once per screen outside the tab bar.
</what_to_give_me>

The bordered ADD-to-stepper control, the Delivery/Dining segmented toggle, and the pull-up hero info card specified with exact geometry and morph timing
House rules protecting the semantic rating discipline, the mandatory dietary mark, and the bordered (never solid) ADD-button convention
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in dual-purpose dining platforms that serve both delivery ordering and in-restaurant discovery from a single detail screen. You think in terms of information-dense scanning, semantic color coding, and mode-switching UI, and you deliver production-ready SwiftUI, not mockups.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (light / dark):
- Canvas: #FFFFFF / #121212 warm near-black (never true black)
- Surface 1/2: #F4F4F5 / #1C1C1E, #EBEBEC / #262629
- Divider: #E8E8E8 / #2C2C2E
- Text primary: #1C1C1C / #F2F2F2
- Text secondary: #696969 / #9C9C9C
- Brand/primary accent: #E23744, pressed #C42531
- Semantic rating scale: green #267E3E (great, ~4.0+), amber #DB7C38 (average, 3.0-3.9), red #E23744 (poor, <3.0, reuses the brand red), gray #9C9C9C (unrated/new)
- Membership gold (sparingly): #EFC75E, dining/reservation blue: #256FEF
- Veg mark green #267E3E, non-veg mark maroon #B91C1C, error #E03A3A

Typography: a dense, heavy grotesque (documented as an Inter-class substitute for a proprietary house face) carries the whole system — screen titles at weight 900, restaurant/venue names at 24pt/800, menu category headers 17pt/800, dish names 15pt/700, prices 14pt/700 tabular. Metadata (cuisine, locality, distance) stays small and muted at 13pt/400 so the name, rating pill, and price lead the eye.

Spacing/geometry: 4pt base, scale 4-8-12-14-16-18-22-24-32-40-48. The hero info card overlaps its photo by -22pt with a matching 22pt top radius. Radius scale: 4pt veg/non-veg mark, 7pt rating pill, 10pt ADD button/stepper/search field, 12pt listing photos/thumbnails, 22pt pull-up info card and bottom sheets, 999px pill for the mode-segmented toggle, 50% circles.

Distinctive patterns:
1. Semantic rating pill — a small colored chip whose fill color IS the rating's quality tier (great/average/poor/unrated), containing a white star and the bold numeric score; appears on cards, headers, and individual dishes, and two pills can appear side-by-side for two different modes (e.g. delivery rating + dining rating) each with its own review-count caption.
2. Veg/non-veg mark — a small bordered square with a centered dot (veg) or triangle (non-veg), mandatory leading element on every dish row.
3. Bordered 'ADD' button — deliberately NOT a solid brand-color fill: a surface-colored button with a thin brand-colored border and brand-colored text, overlapping the dish thumbnail with a soft shadow, that morphs on tap into a bordered quantity stepper of the same style.
4. Delivery/Dining segmented toggle — a pill-shaped two-segment control at the top of a venue's detail screen; the active half fills solid brand color and switching it re-themes the entire screen's content between an ordering menu and a dining/reservation-oriented view.
5. Hero + pull-up info card — a full-bleed venue photo with a rounded info card sliding up over it, carrying the venue name, a dense meta line, and the side-by-side rating pills.
6. Bestseller/offer tags — small amber or brand-colored inline labels calling out popular dishes or active discounts, never used as a background fill.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. The rating pill's fill color must always be computed from the actual score tier (great/average/poor/unrated) — never hardcode a pill color independent of the number, since the color IS the fastest signal in the app.
2. Every dish or menu-item row must carry the veg/non-veg (or locale-appropriate dietary) mark as a mandatory leading element — never make it optional or decorative.
3. The ADD button is always a bordered, surface-colored control with colored text and border — never a solid brand-color fill; only the stepper it morphs into shares that same bordered language.
4. When the product spans two modes on one detail screen (e.g. delivery ordering and in-venue dining), implement it as a single segmented toggle that re-themes the screen's content, not as two separate destinations.
5. Membership/loyalty gold accents are used sparingly and only on dedicated membership surfaces — never spread the gold color into general chrome or navigation.
6. Keep the dark-mode canvas a warm near-black, never a true #000000 — this preserves legibility and warmth in a dense information layout.
7. Type runs dense and heavy by design (venue names at 800 weight, screen titles at 900) with metadata kept small and muted — resist the urge to lighten this for a 'calmer' look, since density-with-hierarchy is the intended read.
8. Never shadow ordinary menu rows or listing cards in light mode — separation comes from photography, dividers, and the semantic pill colors; reserve shadow strictly for floating, tappable elements like the ADD button and sticky cart/pull-up card.
9. Embed the price directly into the primary action button label (e.g. 'Add item · $X.XX') rather than displaying price and button as separate elements.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App/brand name: [your dining/delivery platform]
- Modes to support on a single venue page (e.g. delivery + dine-in, delivery + reservations): [fill in]
- Rating scale and score thresholds for the semantic tiers: [fill in]
- Dietary or allergen marks required in your market: [fill in]
- Offer/discount mechanics (percentage off, free delivery, bestseller tags): [fill in]
- Membership/loyalty tier name if applicable: [fill in]
- Primary accent hex if different from the reference red: [fill in]
- Target iOS minimum version: [fill in]
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete Color and Font SwiftUI extension implementing the palette (including the semantic rating-tier logic) and type ladder, adapted to the given brand.
2. The semantic rating pill component that computes its fill color from a numeric score, including a two-pill side-by-side variant.
3. The bordered ADD button component with its morph-into-stepper animation.
4. The Delivery/Dining (or equivalent two-mode) segmented toggle that re-themes the screen's content on switch.
5. The venue detail header: full-bleed hero photo, transparent nav scrims, and the pull-up info card with the dense meta line and rating pills.
6. The dish/menu-item row with dietary mark, optional bestseller tag, price, and the ADD control.
7. A short motion reference table for the ADD-to-stepper morph, the toggle slide, and the hero pull-up card's scroll behavior.
</what_to_give_me>
